Moving pm.exe breaks its shortcuts: running pm shortcut from its new place makes them again.

docs.title: How pm follows a program
docs.text: The program is launched in a Windows Job Object: every process it creates stays attached to it. Without track, the session ends when the last process of the group has stopped.

docs.title: Launchers
docs.text:
Many programs go through a launcher: dcs_updater.exe starts dcs.exe and exits. track: dcs.exe tells pm to follow that process, by its handle, rather than the launcher:

  • pm finds it in the group as soon as it is created;
  • if it left the group, pm looks for it by name among the processes created after the launch;
  • when it stops, pm waits 3 more seconds, in case it hands over to another process of the same name (Windows 11's Notepad does that);
  • if the launcher still runs (to start the game again after an update, say), pm waits for it and says so in the log;
  • the other processes the game started (a radio client such as SRS, an overlay) are not waited for: the log names them, and kill_on_exit can stop them;
  • if it does not appear within 10 seconds after everything else has ended, the session ends in error.

docs.title: Guards
docs.text:
• Locks: a session takes a lock on its name, and one per live file of its sync lines. Two sessions with the same name, or two configs writing the same live file, cannot run together: the second is refused before any copy. Windows releases the locks when pm exits, even after a crash.
  • Program already running outside pm (if_running), checked on the followed process and on the launcher: abort (default) refuses, nothing is copied or launched; kill stops the existing instances, launcher first, then checks nothing runs any more.
  • Last safety net (with track): if, when the after actions are due, the followed process still runs unfollowed, or the process list cannot be read, the after actions do not run and the session ends in error. A missed copy-back, reported, is better than a profile overwritten while the game runs.
  • Safe copies: written to a temporary file then renamed, never half-written; the previous file is kept as .bak.

docs.title: Logs
docs.text: Each session writes <name>[-<profile>]-<date>-<time>.log in log.dir: pm's steps, the copies, the program's output with capture. Only the log.keep most recent are kept.

docs.title: The notification icon
docs.text:
--tray, or ui: tray in the config, replaces the window with an icon in the notification area, for pm run as for pm watch.

Started from a shortcut, pm gives its console window back at once (set the shortcut to "Minimized" so it does not even show). Started from a terminal, it keeps writing to it, and the double Ctrl+C stays active.

docs.title: What the icon shows
docs.text:
• Colour: green while the program runs, orange during the copies (at the start and at the end) or before a restart, grey when paused, red after an error.
  • Tooltip: the session, the profile and the state.
  • Image: --icon FILE, or icon: in the config, or per profile in profiles:, replaces the disc with your image (.png, or .ico in 32-bit or holding a PNG), with a small dot of the state's colour in its bottom-right corner. An unreadable image is reported in the log, and pm keeps the disc.

docs.title: The menu
docs.text:
• Open the log.
  • Stop and finish: stops the program, then runs the after actions.
  • Detach…: after a confirmation that says what it costs at that moment (cancel at start, end during a restart delay, otherwise leave the program without its copy-back). If the session changes state while the question is shown, it is asked again.
  • In watch: Pause, Resume, Restart.

docs.title: The end of the session
docs.text:
• On failure (an error, or a non-zero exit code in pm run), the icon turns red and a Windows message box says what failed and where the log is.
  • A cancellation you asked for is not a failure: no error box.
  • Otherwise the icon keeps its final state for exit.delay, then goes away; with exit.wait_key: always, a "Session over" box shows.

exec commands do not open in a console window, nor does the launched program once pm has no console.

docs.title: PowerShell and paths
docs.text:
The examples in these docs are written for PowerShell, Windows' default terminal.

  • Starting pm: write .\pm.exe, not pm.exe. PowerShell does not look for programs in the current folder; cmd.exe accepts both forms, so .\ is the only one that works everywhere.

  • Environment variables: $env:USERPROFILE in PowerShell, %USERPROFILE% in cmd.exe. Typed in PowerShell, %USERPROFILE% reaches pm as is, and pm then looks for a folder called %USERPROFILE%:

    .\pm.exe run "$env:USERPROFILE\Saved Games\DCS\Profiles\pm-dcs.yaml" --profile DEV

  • In the YAML config, pm reads the variables itself, with its own syntax: ${env:USERPROFILE}.

docs.title: "another pm session is already active"
docs.text: A session with the same name, or writing the same live files, is already running; the message gives its profile. The lock goes away with the pm process holding it, even after a crash: if it stays, a pm still runs (see the notification icon, or the Task Manager).

docs.title: "… already runs outside this session"
docs.text:
The game, or its launcher, was started without pm. pm refuses so as not to overwrite the settings in use: close the program, or set if_running: kill if that is what you want.

The check goes by the program's name: a very common name (cmd.exe, powershell.exe) is nearly always "already running". Start the real program directly: track does not get around this refusal, since the launched program is checked too.

docs.title: The copy-back did not happen
docs.text: The log says why: session detached (double Ctrl+C, q twice, window closed), or the last safety net (the followed process still ran unfollowed). The live files have not moved: starting the session again and ending it normally copies the settings back.

docs.title: A process the game started stays open
docs.text: pm only waits for the game and its launcher; the other processes (a radio client, an overlay) are named in the log. To stop them at the end, list them in kill_on_exit. A program running as administrator cannot be stopped by a pm started without elevation: the log shows "access denied".

docs.title: The icon does not show my image
docs.text: pm reads .png files and .ico files in 32-bit or holding a PNG. A 256-colour .ico is refused: the log says so, and pm keeps the coloured disc. Use the matching .png, or save the icon again in 32-bit.

docs.title: pm speaks the wrong language
docs.text: pm follows the Windows display language. To force it: the language in the interface's settings (for all of pm), lang: fr in the config, the PM_LANG variable or --lang fr; the exact order is in language.

docs.title: pm watch
docs.text:
.\pm.exe watch <config.yaml> [--profile NAME] [--tray | --no-tui] [--icon FILE] [--lang fr|en]

pm watch restarts the program every time it stops, as watch.restart says: always (default), on-failure (only on a non-zero exit code) or never.

docs.title: Restarts
docs.text:
• A stop less than 10 seconds after the launch counts as a crash loop: the first waits watch.delay, each next one doubles the delay, up to watch.max_delay.
  • watch.max_restarts only counts automatic restarts, not those asked with r.
  • The sync lines are copied once at the start and copied back once at the end of the session.
  • The other before actions (a cleanup, for instance) run again before every restart; the after actions only run at the end.
  • At the end of each run, pm stops what is left of the process group, so leftovers do not pile up from one run to the next.

docs.title: Keys
docs.text:
Key Effect p pauses / resumes the program (all its processes) r stops and restarts the program k stops the program, runs the after actions, quits q twice detaches: pm quits, the program goes on, the after actions do not run; at start, cancels; during the delay before a restart, ends the session, after actions included arrows, PgUp/PgDn scroll the log

--no-tui replaces the interface with a plain text log, for a service for instance. --tray replaces it with the notification icon.

docs.title: Example: back up before starting
docs.text:
The need: before every game, keep a copy of a game's saves, in case a game damages them, without piling up archives forever.

What Process Monitor does:

  1. before the launch, it creates a dated .zip archive of the saves folder;
  2. it starts the game and waits for it to close;
  3. afterwards, it keeps only the 10 most recent archives.

If the archive cannot be created, the game is not started: no playing without a safety net.

docs.title: The config
docs.text:
The comments in the file are in French; the lines are explained below.

# Sauvegarder avant de lancer : pm run backup.yaml
#
# Avant le lancement, une archive datée du dossier de sauvegardes ; à la
# fermeture, on ne garde que les 10 plus récentes.

name: jeu-sauvegarde
lang: fr

vars:
  saves: ${env:USERPROFILE}\Documents\MonJeu\Saves
  archives: ${env:USERPROFILE}\Documents\MonJeu\Archives

command: C:\Jeux\MonJeu\MonJeu.exe

hooks:
  before:
    - exec: [powershell, -NoProfile, -Command, 'New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force ''${archives}'' | Out-Null; Compress-Archive -Path ''${saves}\*'' -DestinationPath (''${archives}\saves-'' + (Get-Date -Format yyyyMMdd-HHmmss) + ''.zip'')']
  after:
    - exec: [powershell, -NoProfile, -Command, 'Get-ChildItem ''${archives}\saves-*.zip'' | Sort-Object Name -Descending | Select-Object -Skip 10 | Remove-Item']
  timeout: 5m

# .\pm.exe shortcut backup.yaml : un raccourci à côté de la config.
shortcuts: { mode: run }
  • The exec actions run PowerShell here. In a YAML single-quoted string, a quote is doubled (''); ${archives} is replaced by Process Monitor before running.
  • timeout: 5m stops a command that does not return.
  • There is no track: the game starts directly, without a launcher.

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
.\pm.exe check .\backup.yaml
.\pm.exe run .\backup.yaml

pm check shows both commands as they will run, variables replaced.

A unique program name

Process Monitor refuses to start when a program with the same name already runs. For a game, that is the guard you want; but a program with a very common name (cmd.exe, powershell.exe) would nearly always be "already running". See Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Example: DCS World with profiles
docs.text:
The need: play DCS World with several sets of settings (a profile for the screen, one for virtual reality, one for mission development), without copying them by hand, and without one profile overwriting another.

What Process Monitor does:

  1. it copies the chosen profile's files (options.lua, export.lua, control bindings) to their place in Saved Games\DCS;
  2. it starts dcs_updater.exe, then follows dcs.exe, which the launcher starts before exiting;
  3. once DCS has closed, it also closes SRS if it runs, then copies the files back into the profile, with the settings changed in game;
  4. if DCS already runs, or another profile is in use, it refuses to start.

docs.title: Prepare the profiles
docs.text:
One folder per profile in Saved Games\DCS\Profiles, holding a copy of the files to follow:

Saved Games\DCS\Profiles\
  DEV\  export.lua  options.lua  joystick.diff.lua
  VR\   export.lua  options.lua
  STD\  export.lua  options.lua
  Icons\ dcs-dev.ico  dcs-vr.ico  dcs.ico

To create a profile, copy DCS's current files (Scripts\export.lua, Config\options.lua…) into its folder.

docs.title: The config
docs.text:
The comments in the file are in French; the lines are explained below.

# DCS World par profils : pm run dcs.yaml --profile DEV
#
# Avant le lancement, les fichiers du profil sont copiés dans DCS ; après la
# fermeture du jeu, ils sont recopiés dans le profil. Refus net si DCS tourne
# déjà, ou si un autre profil est en cours.

name: dcs
lang: fr

vars:
  saved: ${env:USERPROFILE}\Saved Games\DCS
  prof: ${saved}\Profiles\${profile}

command: C:\jeux\DCS World\bin\dcs_updater.exe
workdir: ${prof}
# dcs_updater.exe passe la main à dcs.exe : c'est lui que la session suit.
track: dcs.exe
# SRS démarré par DCS n'a plus d'usage une fois le jeu fermé.
kill_on_exit: [SR-ClientRadio.exe]
capture: true
ready: { file: '${saved}\dcs.lock', timeout: 3m }

ui: tray
log: { dir: '${prof}\logs', keep: 3 }

hooks:
  sync:
    - ${prof}\export.lua  <-> ${saved}\Scripts\export.lua
    - ${prof}\options.lua <-> ${saved}\Config\options.lua

profiles:
  DEV:
    icon: ${saved}\Profiles\Icons\dcs-dev.ico
    hooks:
      sync:
        - '${prof}\joystick.diff.lua <-> ${saved}\Config\Input\UiLayer\joystick\joystick.diff.lua'
  VR:
    icon: ${saved}\Profiles\Icons\dcs-vr.ico
  STD:
    icon: ${saved}\Profiles\Icons\dcs.ico

exit: { delay: 2s }

# .\pm.exe shortcut dcs.yaml : un raccourci par profil, à côté de la config.
shortcuts:
  mode: run
  name: DCS - ${profile}

Line by line:

  • name: dcs: the three profiles share one lock; two cannot run at once.
  • prof is the folder of the profile chosen with --profile.
  • track: dcs.exe: the session follows the game, not the launcher.
  • kill_on_exit: SRS, started by DCS, is closed with it.
  • ready: the log notes when DCS has finished starting (the dcs.lock file appears).
  • sync: two files common to every profile; DEV adds a third.
  • ui: tray and a per-profile icon:: no console window, an icon in the profile's image.
  • lang: fr: pm speaks French; set en, or remove the line to follow Windows.

docs.title: Check, then run
docs.text:
.\pm.exe check .\dcs.yaml --profile DEV
.\pm.exe run .\dcs.yaml --profile DEV

pm check reports a missing profile file before anything is launched.

docs.title: One shortcut per profile
docs.text:
The config's shortcuts section describes them; one command creates them all:

.\pm.exe shortcut .\dcs.yaml

Each one has these settings:

  • Target: C:\...\pm.exe run "C:\...\dcs.yaml" --profile DEV
  • Start in: the config's folder
  • Run: Minimized
  • Icon: the same as the profile's (Icons\dcs-dev.ico)

A double-click starts DCS with that profile; the icon shows in the notification area and goes away once the settings are back.

docs.title: Example: keep SimAppPro alive
docs.text:
The need: SimAppPro, the software driving simulation devices, must run for the whole gaming session; if it crashes, it must be restarted, and its temporary files pile up.

What Process Monitor does:

  1. it stops a SimAppPro instance already running, to start from a known state;
  2. it cleans the temporary files, then starts SimAppPro;
  3. every time it stops, it restarts it, cleaning first; if it crashes in a loop, it spaces the restarts out up to one minute;
  4. when the session is stopped, it cleans one last time.

docs.title: The config
docs.text:
The comments in the file are in French; the lines are explained below.

# Garder SimAppPro en vie : pm watch simapppro.yaml
#
# Toute instance déjà lancée est arrêtée ; les fichiers temporaires sont
# nettoyés avant chaque lancement et à la fin de la session.

name: simapppro
lang: fr

command: ${env:LOCALAPPDATA}\Programs\SimAppPro\SimAppPro.exe
workdir: ${config_dir}
if_running: kill
capture: true
env:
  ELECTRON_NO_ATTACH_CONSOLE: "true"   # SimAppPro est une appli Electron

ui: tray
icon: ${env:LOCALAPPDATA}\Programs\SimAppPro\resources\icon.png
log: { dir: '${config_dir}\logs', keep: 2 }

watch:
  restart: always
  delay: 2s
  max_delay: 1m

hooks:
  before:
    - delete: ${config_dir}\Scripts
    - delete: ${config_dir}\WWTHID.log
    - delete: ${config_dir}\WWTUSBHID.log
  after:
    - delete: ${config_dir}\Scripts
    - delete: ${config_dir}\WWTHID.log
    - delete: ${config_dir}\WWTUSBHID.log

# .\pm.exe shortcut simapppro.yaml : un raccourci sur le Bureau.
shortcuts: { mode: watch, name: SimAppPro, folder: '${desktop}' }
  • if_running: kill: an instance already running is stopped instead of blocking the start.
  • capture: true and ELECTRON_NO_ATTACH_CONSOLE: SimAppPro's output goes to the log, without opening a console.
  • watch: always restart, 2 seconds after the stop, up to one minute for a crash series.
  • hooks.before runs again before every restart; hooks.after only runs at the end of the session.
  • ui: tray and icon:: SimAppPro's icon in the notification area, with the state dot. If the image file does not exist on your machine, pm says so in the log and keeps the coloured disc.

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
.\pm.exe watch .\simapppro.yaml

The icon's menu pauses, restarts, stops or detaches. In a console, without ui: tray, the same actions are on the p, r, k and q keys (see pm watch).
